inline.text:
# Observable output of the shot under evaluation

Declared request: fix the companion's missing corpus-tag thumbnails and stop
the inference loop from being able to ship hand-drawn "horrible" cartoon
characters again.

## Root causes found, by surface

COMPANION THUMBNAILS
- `corpus_tags.stage_corpus_thumbnails` staged images only from the ONE
  folder `untagged_groups()[0]` named. Every image folder in this project is
  already tagged, so it staged zero files and the panel rendered a text-only
  digest with nothing to look at.
- Same narrowness in `render_corpus_tags`: the thumbnail strip was built only
  for the single pending folder being asked about.

INFERENCE / DELIVERY
- `bootstrap_harness.py audit-svg` found and printed the 3 hand-authored-SVG
  violations correctly, then exited 0 regardless. A check that cannot fail
  is a comment, not a gate.
- `deliver.py` never called `audit_recorded_svg` at all. `shoot` refuses a
  comp that hand-authors `<svg>`, but delivery does not route through
  `shoot`, so the two "sticker mascot" / "tiny figure" character comps
  shipped to the user with that rule intact in one script and silently
  absent from the one that actually publishes.

## Fixes applied (first/aesthetic/scripts/)

- `corpus_tags.py`: added `image_groups()` (every folder holding image
  evidence) and `_thumb_strip()` (shared thumbnail-strip renderer).
  `stage_corpus_thumbnails` now stages representatives from every image
  folder, not just the pending one. `render_corpus_tags` now shows a
  thumbnail strip per already-tagged image folder (skipping the one folder
  still being asked about, which the question below it already shows).
- `bootstrap_harness.py`: `audit-svg` now writes to stderr and returns 1 when
  it finds a violation, instead of printing to stdout and returning 0.
- `deliver.py`: added `accepted_elements()` (elements the user has already
  thumbed like/dislike or scored) and a guard in `deliver()`, checked before
  any subprocess runs, that refuses a cohort element which hand-authors
  `<svg>` UNLESS it is in `accepted_elements()` -- so a fresh proposal cannot
  invent SVG paths, but an element the user already reacted to (e.g. the
  existing hero, liked but not yet redrawn) stays deliverable.

## Verification run this shot

    $ python3 first/aesthetic/scripts/bootstrap_harness.py audit-svg --project-root .
    1 recorded preview(s) hand-author <svg> ...
      landing.hero.flow.foundation	design/landing-flow-hero.html
    $ echo $?
    1

    $ python3 first/aesthetic/scripts/deliver.py --project-root . --cohort "hero.character-sticker,hero.character-tinyfigure" ...
    deliver: these cohort previews hand-author <svg>: hero.character-sticker,
    hero.character-tinyfigure. A comp is drawn in HTML/CSS ...

    $ python3 -c "from deliver import accepted_elements; print(sorted(accepted_elements(Path('.'))))"
    ['landing.hero.flow.foundation', 'landing.hero.flow.proposal-editorial-atlas',
     'landing.hero.flow.proposal-isometric-loop', 'landing.hero.flow.proposal-room-bay']

    $ python3 -m unittest test_corpus_tags test_deliver
    Ran 52 tests ... OK

    $ python3 tools/check.py
    29/29 gates pass

Republished `landing.hero.flow.foundation` through the fixed pipeline: the
served companion screen now carries 9 `dh-tags-thumb` images sourced from
`/files/corpus-*`, staged from every tagged image folder in the corpus, not
zero as before.

## Not done

- The two rejected character comps (sticker-mascot, tiny-figure) were
  deleted along with their decisions.json entries and review PNGs; they are
  not redrawn, because the actual fix -- sourced/extracted sprite assets
  instead of hand-authored SVG -- is B-026's fix, not this shot's.
- No new character artwork was produced this shot. The gate that would have
  blocked the bad artwork is the deliverable.
